design_rationale:
TASK 1 DOSSIER — contents_packout_and_storage (env_0079), revision after policy audit round 5 and KB audit revisions 1 and 3 (rework round 8). The site-wait rule keys on the rebuild contract's status alone (substantially_complete -> open-site wait, final_invoiced -> invoiced-site wait); it states no punch-list or closing-visit condition. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts [6, 6, 6, 6]; every problem takes 6.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Paul Ostrander asks only to "settle up what I owe on the contents job" after his High-Value packout came home on 2026-10-20. The closing payment rule waits, in three prerequisite sentences, on the three move-back lines of the return (pack-back boxes, furniture reset, truck loads), none of which stands at the opening. The agent must find the three pricing rules, price each line from the job's packout, disposal and storage records, the company rebuild contract read at the same address on the job's claim file (condo_unit, substantially complete 2026-10-08), the linked fire job (moderate smoke) and the claim file (policy state FL), book them, and then price the closing payment, whose overrun above the carrier's approved contents scope moves with every one of the three lines.

SCOPE (Principle C). Task 0 holds the in-custody customer vault, coverage and share rules. Task 1 claims contents_ext_pack_back_box_line / charge_pack_back_boxes_26b5c86b, contents_ext_furniture_reset_line / charge_furniture_reset_9904d302, contents_ext_return_truck_loads / charge_return_truck_loads_2b0047ce (the move-back lines of a return, all storage tiers) and contents_ext_closing_payment / pay_contents_closing_balance_f918d993 (closing payment on insurance-funded jobs in returned or invoiced status, arrangements other than Homeowner Direct Pay, no customer line past the referral days). The claims-charter rules both payments honour are worded separately in each rule.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root D1 = contents_ext_closing_payment (owner=user). Edges, all value_input on excess_share, state form: D1 -> pack-back box line: "The closing payment is not figured until the job carries the pack-back box line owed for its return." (negated); D1 -> furniture reset line: "The closing payment is not taken until the furniture reset line owed for the return stands on the job." (negated); D1 -> truck loads: "The closing payment is fixed only after the truck loads that brought the contents home stand on the job as a move-back line." (affirmative). Each state is booked by exactly one tool of this difficulty. False at opening: status returned, returned_date 2026-10-20, no move-back line among the job's charges. Deletion runs: skip boxes -> 5301.77; skip reset -> 7495.96; skip loads -> 8125.05 (payment 8930.89). The three lines commute (no pricing rule of a move-back line reads another move-back line). Persona names no prerequisite; tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Move-back lines: contents_pack_back_charge, governed by contents_return with no eligibility gate for that subject (policy_scope); billed after the recorded return. Return truck loads are a move-back line (code truck_trip); the truck rule declares overrides of three clauses of contents_evt_packout_and_cleaning for that line only, restating each for every other line: 'Truck trips are billed per load' (the inventory-report clause of that sentence stays in force), 'Amounts are quantity times unit rate' (the half-up rounding stays in force), and the status sentence 'The job must be in authorized, in_custody or return_scheduled status when a packout, cleaning or disposal line is charged.' (the move-back truck line is charged once the job is returned). The box and reset rules each retire the base pack-back pricing sentence for their own line, naming the sibling lines. Payment: py_state (status returned). Referral scope: every coverage line dated on or before 2026-08-24 is paid after the 2026-08-20 ACH payment; the unpaid customer lines (2026-09-06 and 2026-10-06 periods) are under the High-Value tier's 60 referral days. No time gate.

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. One contents job (High-Value, Unit 3B). Closing inputs: customer-billed lines cv6, cv7, ov6, ov7, va0..va7 (5060.00), surcharges sur1/sur2 (53.10), payments pay1..pay3 (2700.00), no refund, no billing_error or duplicate_line credit, custody credit cc1 (240.00); contents work charged = packout lines, haul and the three move-back lines (16129.12); claim: approvals ap_init 10600.00 and ap_supp 1900.00 (naming request rq_supp, contents_added supplement number 1, 2600.00, so the highest-numbered request is decided), ap_init withholds 600.00 recoverable depreciation; write-offs ap_wo 407.00 carrier_denied_line and ap_dep 600.00 depreciation_forfeited (posted 2026-10-02, after the 180-day window from the 2026-03-31 ACV payment closed on 2026-09-27; no release request, and the contents job was not complete until 2026-10-20); payments cp_cd 9400.00 ACV contractor_direct (received 2026-03-31, posted as post1 on 2026-04-01) and cp_io 2000.00 ACV insured_only; carrier receivable 93.00; most recent insurance storage lines cv5 645.00 and ov5 85.00 (2026-08-07); returned 2026-10-20; the rebuild contract records no work suspension.

FACTOR CARD (tier / single-factor baseline figure / all-baseline).
Pack-back boxes 4298.80 (3088.80): unit_carry (CROSS rebuild) condo 8% -> 4051.70; new_floor_protection (CROSS rebuild date) 12-day lead -> 1.40/box -> 3971.20; wardrobe_hanging (method) 18 boxes, below 20, standard 18 x 5.50 -> 4199.80; high_value_condition_check (method) 22 items per item 8.75 -> 4106.30; odor_barrier_bagging (CROSS fire) moderate 1.10/box -> 4041.40; heavy_box_handling (method) 72 boxes, graduated 60 x 1.25 + 12 x 0.95 = 86.40 -> 4212.40. Volume ladders are graduated (the volume charge applies only to boxes beyond the threshold), so a larger quantity never costs less. Boxes brought back 264 - 30 signed = 234 is a plain rule (part of the standard method).
Furniture reset 1434.93 (880.40): reset_unit_carry 8% -> 1364.50; reset_floor_runners 2.10 -> 1369.83; odor_film_unwrap 2.75 -> 1349.68; oversized_set_crew single 145.00 -> 1289.93; second_reset_crew (method) 31 items per piece 3.25 -> 1334.18; crate_uncrating 4 x 22.00 -> 1346.93. Pieces set = 31 furniture items (plain).
Truck loads 805.84 (645.00): return_load_count (method) ceil(234/120)=2 -> 1126.26; air_ride_truck 8% -> 768.00; state_trip_schedule (CROSS claims) FL 1.10 -> 759.40; rebuild_site_wait (CROSS rebuild) 35.00 -> 735.84; unit_delivery_access 30.00 -> 745.84; oversized_move_truck 165.00 -> 640.84.
Closing payment 8930.89 (2413.10): contents_scope_overrun (method, CROSS claims, multi-condition) 16129.12 - 12500.00 -> 5301.77; insured_money_pass_on (method) min(2000.00, 12500.00 - 407.00 - 9400.00) -> 6930.89; declined_lines_dispute (parameter) disputed 0 -> 407.00 carried -> 8523.89; unpaid_storage_tail (parameter) 5 days x 730.00/30 -> 8809.22; owed_compensation_netting (method) custody 240.00 stands -> custody and goodwill (0.00) netted in full -> 9170.89; withheld_depreciation_carry (parameter, CROSS claims) billable arrangement, forfeited write-off 600.00 -> 8330.89. Ledger closure: balance after the four writes 13282.22 - 8930.89 = 4351.33 = carrier receivable 93.00 + insurance-billed storage 4380.00 less the 121.67 tail (residue -0.0033, the half-up rounding of 8930.886667).
Near-misses: recorded vault count 3 for loads; the March packout truck_trip line (3 loads) is a packout line, not the return line; the 1900.00 supplement approval decides the 2600.00 request, so nothing awaits; the contractor_direct payment is already posted; the forfeited depreciation is a write-off (not an approval), and the 93.00 receivable is still owed by the carrier.
XF A1 / A2 / A7: factors read only their own bindings plus plain reads (box_rate, boxes_back, pieces_set, trip_fee, customer lines; insurer_storage_lines and denied_writeoffs belong to the tail and declined-lines factors; the vault capacity and boxes packed belong to return_load_count and the period length to unpaid_storage_tail, the only factors reading them); combination sentences name only generic quantities. Method pairs: high_value_condition_check {items x hours x technician rate (tariff), items x per-item charge, none}; second_reset_crew {items x hours x technician rate, items x per-piece add, none}; return_load_count {haul-adjusted ceil, capacity ceil, recorded}; contents_scope_overrun, insured_money_pass_on (as in task 0; the pass-on leaves depreciation releases to withheld_depreciation_carry); owed_compensation_netting {custody credits + goodwill credits in full, min(goodwill, customer's own charges) (adds the own-charges input and the lesser-of pick), none}. Rebuild reads take, at the job's loss address and on the job's own claim file, the contract furthest along and never a cancelled one. Overlap: overrun on non-storage work, tail after the approved end, pass-on capped by approved scope less write-offs and postings; the most recent contents_added request is the highest supplement number.
Probe table (scratch): no rebuild contract -> carry, protection, runners, wait and access 0; a cancelled proposal listed first -> live contract still read (same figures); completion after the return -> no protection or runners; heavy smoke -> 1.85/box; 30 high-value items -> technician time; 45 furniture items -> hourly second crew; goodwill 500 without custody, own charges 5113.10 -> netted 500; goodwill 400 without custody on a job whose storage is all billed to the carrier (own charges 0) -> nothing netted; custody 240 with goodwill 500 -> netted 740; no forfeited write-off -> nothing carried (carrier still owes the 600.00); forfeited write-off on Assignment of Benefits -> nothing carried; release 600.00 paid insured_only -> 600.00 carried; release paid contractor_direct -> nothing carried; forfeited write-off on the dwelling coverage -> not read; price_variance request awaiting -> write-off less the request; price_variance request decided at 300 -> write-off carried in full, overrun less 300; refund 100 -> +100; billing_error credit 450 -> -450; boxes packed 0 -> boxes brought back floored at zero; contents_added request with no approval -> overrun less the request; two contents_added requests on the same date -> the higher supplement number is read; a second rebuild contract on another claim file at the same address -> not read.

PERSONA. Friendly retired band director; volunteers the return date and the wish to settle up; phone 8505550463 and ZIP 32503; claim number, email, the $2,000 check and the credited lamp only when asked; agrees to charges that must be added first; pays the stated amount himself by bank transfer (ach, no surcharge); closes after the confirmation.

STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers -> verify -> find_contents_jobs -> find_contents_charges -> find_contents_payments -> find_contents_disposal_authorizations -> find_claims_files -> find_claims_approvals -> find_claims_payments -> find_claims_requests -> find_rebuild_contracts -> find_fire_jobs -> unlock/call boxes (2026-10-20, 4298.80) -> unlock/call reset (1434.93) -> unlock/call loads (805.84) -> unlock_user/call_user closing payment (ach, 8930.89, surcharge 0.00). Recomputed by scratch sens.py through check_compute's evaluator.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. The three prerequisite sentences send the agent to the job's charge lines, where no move-back line exists; the three pricing rules give the figures from records the finders return; the closing payment follows. Object, date (returned_date) and tender (bank transfer) admit one reading.

BLUEPRINT-KNOWN candidates: the customer's only computable write is a payment; several move-back levers are company schedules with policy parameters keyed on rebuild, fire and packout records. Fire, rebuild and dwelling-claim ledgers are not seeded because no gold read returns them (replay closure).
user_scenario:
You are Paul Ostrander, a retired high-school band director who owns a condo at 4418 Osceola Bluff Road, Unit 3B, in Pensacola. A kitchen fire in March filled the unit with smoke; Ridgecrest Restoration cleaned up, packed out your belongings — the piano, your framed prints, the good china — and rebuilt the kitchen. Your things came back on Tuesday, October 20, and you have spent the week unpacking. You are friendly and talkative, but you like to get bills settled promptly and you want to close this chapter.

You open with something like: "Good morning! My belongings came back home on Tuesday, and I'd like to settle up what I owe on the contents job so we can put this whole thing behind us."

When the representative asks you to confirm who you are, you give your phone number, 8505550463, and your ZIP code, 32503. Only if asked for more, your email is paul.ostrander@gmail.com and your insurance claim number is OCI-HO-26-4682 with Osprey Coast Insurance. If asked whether Osprey Coast paid you anything directly for your contents, you say yes, they sent you a check for $2,000 in June. If asked about any damage, you mention that one lamp came back with a cracked base and that Ridgecrest already put a credit on your account for it. You do not know how the bill is put together and you say so cheerfully if asked.

You are fine with the representative adding whatever charges still belong on the contents job: if you are told something has to be put on the account first, you say "Sure, go right ahead." You will not read any account numbers out loud. When the representative tells you the amount and sends you the secure payment option, you pay exactly that amount yourself by bank transfer from your checking account. If asked how you'd like to pay, you say a bank transfer from checking.

Once the payment has gone through and the representative confirms it, you thank them warmly and say goodbye. If the representative tells you the amount before sending the payment option, you wait for the payment option and then pay it.
